item.title: Bills make decision on C.J. Gardner-Johnson after spitting incident
item.description: CBS C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s decision to spit on Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers will cost him a game on the field and some money in his pocket, but not his roster spot with the Buffalo Bills. Gardner-Johnson, who was issued a one-game suspension by the NFL for his transgression, will not be cut, Bills head coach Joe Brady confirmed on Monday. “Look, C.J.’s a member of the Buffalo Bills,” Brady told reporters when asked about the veteran safety’s status. “We brought him here for a reason , and we know that he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team, and, you know, just like everybody else, right, we’ve got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes.” CJGJ apologizes Gardner-Johnson spit on Bowers during a confrontation in the second half of Buffalo’s 33-30 win at Allegiant Stadium Sunday. In a statement released Monday, he apologized for his actions. “I want to take a moment to address my actions and sincerely apologize to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me,” Gardner-Johnson wrote . “My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed. The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game. “There is no excuse for my actions, and I take full accountability. No matter how emotional or intense the competition gets, I have to hold myself to a higher standard.” The Bills have a bye this weekend, meaning Gardner-Johnson will have to sit out the team’s Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens on Nov. 1. item.title: It's official, Liverpool's new Trent Alexander-Arnold joins Andoni Iraola's first-team
item.description: It's official, Liverpool's new Trent Alexander-Arnold joins Andoni Iraola's first-team An exciting new player has joined Andoni Iraola's first-team, he could be the next Trent Alexander-Arnold. That Alexander-Arnold announcement video was soul-crushing. The awkward sit-down, the sigh, the sad expression. It was all incredibly disappointing. For over a year, it felt like Trent had been stringing Liverpool fans along. He celebrated silencing his critics and made comments that gave supporters hope, seemingly all while knowing his future lay elsewhere. The Scouser who could have become this generation’s Steven Gerrard instead risked becoming another Michael Owen. His decision to leave damaged his relationship with the fans and tarnished the legacy he could have built at Anfield. Trent had everything needed to become a Liverpool legend. Instead, he chose a different path, one that has so far failed to deliver the success he might have expected. Liverpool's homegrown issues and how it all started Alexander-Arnold’s departure also seemed to set a precedent for other academy players. In the year or so since he left, several others have followed him out of the door. Tyler Morton moved on, Jarell Quansah left, and Curtis Jones also departed. Like Trent, these were players who had been at Liverpool from a young age, worked their way through the academy and eventually established themselves in the first team. Yet, they all ended up leaving Anfield. That sparked concerns over Liverpool’s identity, with the possibility of the Reds heading into the new season without a Scouser or a genuine academy graduate in their senior squad. It’s been a talking point ever since, but Liverpool might just be on the verge of finding their next Alexander-Arnold. Liverpool's new Alexander-Arnold joins Andoni Iraola's first-team The Reds' new Spanish coach seems a lot more open to involving the academy players from the squad. This has already allowed for opportunities for the likes of Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Luke Chambers. All of these players came from Liverpool's academy but none of them are technically scousers. Since Jones left the club, Liverpool have been in search of a new scouser in the team. Well, the Reds might not have to wait much longer. Jayden Danns joined Iraola's first-team in training ahead of Liverpool's trip to Villareal. It's another big call-up for the exciting forward. It's not the first-team he's joined the first-team but the fact that he is with the first-team again is a good sign. If he just overcomes his injury problems, he could very well be the Reds' new Alexander-Arnold in the sense that he will be the scouser and the fan favourite in the team.

item.title: Alaba already injured after first start of Udinese career
item.description: Alaba already injured after first start of Udinese career Udinese have confirmed that former Bayern Munich and Real Madrid defender David Alaba is facing a spell on the sidelines after picking up an injury immediately after his first start for the club. Udinese confirm injury to Alaba after first Serie A start Alaba joined Udinese on a free transfer at the end of September following a brief spell as a free agent after the expiry of his contract with Real Madrid on June 30. Official: David Alaba joins Udinese (@udinesecalcio via X) He was introduced for his Serie A debut off the bench during Udinese’s 2-1 defeat against Torino in the first game back after the international break and was included in Kosta Runjaic’s starting XI for the first time for Sunday’s eventual 3-0 defeat against Lecce. Alaba was withdrawn at half-time of Sunday’s defeat against Lecce and Udinese have since confirmed that he has suffered a muscular strain in his right calf. The club writes in a statement that “the player has already begun the rehabilitation process and will be evaluated weekly.” The club has not specified an exact recovery time, but the 34-year-old will be ruled out of Udinese’s upcoming Serie A match at home against Milan on Sunday. The away match against Parma next Wednesday seems unlikely at this stage as well. La Gazzetta dello Sport suggests that Alaba could be out of action until the next international break, which officially kicks off on November 9.

item.title: Tottenham set to rival Barcelona in pursuit of highly-rated Brazilian defender – report
item.description: Tottenham set to rival Barcelona in pursuit of highly-rated Brazilian defender – report Barcelona, under Deco and Joao Amaral, have expanded their scouting network and are aiming to sign foreign starlets early in their development. The likes of Hamza Abdelkarim and Jesse Bisiwu represent such investments, with Barça choosing to trust in their potential. One such player the club are interested in for the future is Brazilian defender Arthur Dias. item.title: Nankivell opens Ireland door with new contract
item.description: Alex Nankivell joined Munster in 2023 from the Chiefs in his native New Zealand [Getty Images] Munster centre Alex Nankivell has signed a new contract with Munster until 2029, which opens the door to international eligibility with Ireland. The 29-year-old joined Munster from the Chiefs in his native New Zealand in 2023 and, through World Rugby's eligibility rules, could play for Ireland in the autumn of 2028. Nankivell, who has previously played for the Maori All Blacks and an All Blacks XV, would be 31 by the time he is eligible to play for Andy Farrell's side. Since moving to Munster, Nankivell has established himself as a key player and bounced back from an injury-hit 2024-25 campaign to be named the province's player of the season in June. Ian Costello, general manager of Munster, said that Nankivell is a "highly valued and repsected member of the squad. "He has made a massive contribution both on and off the pitch since joining Munster," said Costello. "We are delighted that he has committed his future to the club and look forward to seeing him continue to develop as a player and build on his performances in a Munster jersey. "He has ambitions to play at international level, and we hope to see him realise that potential in the near future."

item.title: You won’t believe how long Junior Caminero’s HR trot lasted
item.description: Junior Caminero is the best player on the chronically underrated Tampa Bay Rays . At 23 years old, he is one of the brightest young stars in the game. And like so many greats before him, Caminero has raised his game to meet the biggest moments. The third baseman showed a penchant for clutch hitting as the Rays took control of the American League Championship Series, taking three straight against the Cleveland Guardians to earn a World Series berth . He’ll now get the opportunity to shine on the biggest stage. MORE: Updated World Series schedule immediately announced: Rays win 2026 ALCS Those unfamiliar with his game will soon learn that he plays with immense confidence and passion. He’ll do something amazing on the field and then make sure everyone knows about it, as is his right. Oct 19, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero (13) reacts after hitting a home run during the seventh inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Caminero’s historic home run trot For evidence, look no further than his exploits on Monday night. Caminero roped a two-run homer in the seventh inning to double Tampa Bay’s lead en route to a 7-3 victory. Then he took his sweet time rounding the bases. Caminero took every chance to celebrate and savor the moment with a trot that clocked in at 38.66 seconds. Only one player has taken a more leisurely trip in the Statcast era. Junior Caminero took 38.66 seconds to round the bases. Second-slowest time in the Statcast era on an undisputed homer/uninterrupted trot, per @SlangsOnSports. (Via: @MLB) https://t.co/i3uPZVVXOd — Foul Territory (@FoulTerritoryTV) October 20, 2026 It takes some work to take that long to travel 360 feet. The key to encroaching on 40 seconds on the ol’ stop watch is to take a few breaks along the way. Let Caminero’s majestic and glacial pace serve as a reminder to the next player who blasts a clutch dinger. Everything you see is a potential character in the story. Every time you stop to fire up anything along the way, well, the clock just keeps on running. Interrogating my own soul watching this delightful clip reveals something interesting. It feels like at every point prior in history a trot like Caminero put on display would bring a lot of hand-wringing from the baseball purists and diehards. I can say that because I used to be one of them. Five years ago this bit of showmanship would have gotten under my skin. So it’s refreshing to look around at the marketplace of ideas and conclude that we’re all sort of past the need to complain and moan about a guy making a meal of his home run trot. Along the way it became clear that we simply do not need to clutch pearls. And it’s better. It’s great to just enjoy things and to let a slugger enjoy the fruits of their titanic blast without rushing to pen a thinkpiece or chastise them for not playing the right way. Heck, take longer next time. It’s fine.

item.title: Former Norwich and Finland striker Pukki to retire
item.description: Pukki ranks fourth on Norwich City's all-time goalscoring list [Getty Images] Former Norwich City and Finland striker Teemu Pukki has announced his retirement from football at the age of 36. Pukki, who quit international duty last year, is Finland's men's all-time top scorer with 43 goals in 133 matches, while his number of caps is the country's second highest. He scored 88 goals in 210 appearances for Norwich between 2018 and 2023, helping the Canaries twice win promotion to the Premier League. "I've gained a lot more from football than I ever dreamed of when I was a little boy." Pukki wrote on Instagram. "I've seen the world and gained experience because of football and I don't think I could have gotten anything like football anywhere else. "It hasn't always been fun or I haven't been able to enjoy it, but the love for football has remained - always. Big thanks to the great clubs and their fans." He has played for HJK Helsinki in his homeland since 2025 and will retire following the conclusion of the Veikkausliiga season on 8 November. Pukki also counts Schalke, Brondby and Minnesota United among his former clubs, while he also scored nine goals in 38 appearances for Celtic between 2013 and 2015. Pukki party memories will live on - analysis There was a time when if you told a stranger you were a Norwich fan they would reply with, "Jeremy Goss!" In the last few years that has been replaced with, "Teemu Pukki!" The unassuming Finn arrived on a free transfer in the summer of 2018 to very little fanfare. Pukki's previous foray into British football had been with Celtic and their supporters were quick to tell Norwich fans that their new acquisition wasn't up to much. They could not have been more wrong. With the help of one Emi Buendia teeing him up, Pukki cemented himself as an all-time Norwich great, winning two Championship titles, two player of the season awards and sits fourth among the club's all-time leading scorers. That partnership with Buendia was the stuff of dreams for Norwich supporters and was described as "magical" by head coach Daniel Farke. Thank you, Teemu. You will always be welcome to throw a 'Pukki Party' in Norfolk. Latest Norwich City news and analysis

item.title: Real Madrid boss Mourinho’s blueprint to destabilise Barcelona in El Clasico – report
item.description: Real Madrid boss Mourinho’s blueprint to destabilise Barcelona in El Clasico – report Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid stare at a massive week ahead, with a big UEFA Champions League game midweek and El Clasico scheduled for the weekend. Los Blancos , in that sense, have found momentum at the best possible time as they played one of their best games of the season against Sevilla, and now believe they can take down Barcelona. That does, however, come with the natural sense of caution that Barcelona’s run of form brings. Given how the Catalans are unbeaten in La Liga heading into the Clasico , Mourinho is making big plans to ensure they drop points on the night. Attacking dynamisation As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho wants his attacking department to be unpredictable and versatile against Barcelona such that Hansi Flick’s men are left stunned at what has hit them. Mourinho believes in his attack. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Despite Vinicius Jr. being unavailable, the manager has strong options in Kylian Mbappe, Yan Diomande, Jude Bellingham and Endrick – all of whom started against Sevilla and are expected to continue against Barcelona. The manager wants each player to move differently in the attack to bamboozle Barcelona’s high line so that his side can capitalize and strike on the counter. Diomande, in that sense, is seen as a crucial weapon down the left-flank, and the manager sees that Barcelona will place a special emphasis on defending against the new signing. The idea is that the Catalans will be forced to double-mark the player, thereby opening up central spaces. If Diomande can attract attention on himself, the spaces that open up between the centre-backs will make Kylian Mbappe all the more lethal. Added to that, the manager has asked Jude Bellingham to step up from between the lines and make runs into the box to create jeopardy. Endrick is the wild card Endrick may start against Barcelona. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The Spanish outlet also claims that the manager sees Endrick as a wild card player who can end up making a massive difference, especially given his versatility. If the Brazilian youngster starts, he will feature on the right wing, where he usually does not play. However, he has the ability to play as a winger and also to cut in and threaten as a central presence – something the manager is looking to capitalize on. Endrick’s presence and ability to attract defenders out wide, alongside Diomande’s threat on the left, should create spaces in the centre that Real Madrid hope can make the game for them. Mourinho’s entire idea for the Clasico revolves around counter-attacks, for the manager sees that to be the best way in which his side can hurt the league leaders. Arda Guler and Dean Huijsen are also seen as crucial pillars in the dynamics in that sense.

item.title: Rams’ Sean McVay tries to clean up Kyren Williams mess after his shot across bow
item.description: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Rams’ Sean McVay tries to clean up Kyren Williams mess after his shot across bow appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams are in danger of completely falling apart after Week 6. LA is 2-4 after losing to Arizona and the team looks completely lost despite having a loaded roster. Emotions are already starting to boil over in the locker room, even if there is not full blown revolt. Rams head coach Sean McVay said that he did speak with Kyren Williams about his recent comments following Week 6. McVay claimed that Williams misspoke while emotional after the game. “I have,” McVay told reporters on Monday, per Mike Florio of PFT. “He brought it up to me. I wasn’t aware of it. He’s such an energy for us. He was emotional after the game. I know this guy’s heart. He wants to make sure that he’s influencing and effecting positive change. I think what he said it was more of, ‘I just always want to try to be that spark.’” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Williams was asked why the Rams couldn’t sustain momentum from drive to drive after the loss. He replied “can’t tell you, bro. Probably because I’m not out there.” His comment does seem like a clear shot at the coaching staff. Still, McVay is adamant that Williams’ emotions simply got the better of him in that moment. “He was frustrated after the game, but his teammates know what he’s about. When he explained it to me, I totally understood where he was coming from,” McVay added He’s a great leader for us. I think the way that it was interpreted was not what his intentions were. I know his teammates and I felt that way. He actually brought that up to me on his own. I was not aware of it until he brought it up to me.” The Rams need to figure out how to deal more damage on offense if they want to turn the season around. Unfortunately, that will be more difficult without Davante Adams for several weeks . Next up for the Rams is a Week 7 road game against the Raiders. item.title: Here's the complete list of LPGA players dinged for slow play in 2026
item.description: Carlota Ciganda – or as one fan called her, Carlota 'Slowganda' – made headlines after receiving a two-stroke penalty for slow play while in the mix at the Buick LPGA Shanghai. Ciganda, a repeat offender, ultimately placed fifth. American Yealimi Noh was also dinged two shots on Saturday in China for exceeding the allotted time. While Ciganda and Noh were the first of 2026 to receive two-stroke penalties for slow play, they are hardly alone in costly strokes. A total of five players have received one-stroke penalties thus far in 2026, and two of those players went on to lose by one stroke. South Korea's Jin Hee Im lost in a playoff at the JM Eagle LA Championship after receiving a one-stroke penalty on Saturday for slow play. A few months later, Aprichaya Yubol lost the ShopRite LPGA Classic by one stroke one day after receiving a one-stroke penalty for slow play. Here are the remaining three players that have received one-stroke penalties this season for violating to the tour's Pace-of-Play Policy: Victoria Cui (amateur), Mizuho Americas Open (AJGA); Cocona Sakurai, Lotte Championship; Ziyan Meng (amateur), Buick LPGA Shanghai. The LPGA introduced a stricter pace-of-play policy in 2025 that gives a fine for those who are 1-5 seconds over; a one-stroke penalty for those 6-15 seconds over; and a two-stroke penalty for more than 16 seconds. The new policy went into effect at the Ford Championship last spring. From March 2025 to this point, there have been eight one-stroke penalties and four two-stroke penalties. The last time the PGA Tour handed one a slow-play penalty was the 2017 Zurich Classic, a team event. Prior to that, Glen Day was the most recent player to receive a slow-play penalty at the 1995 Honda Classic. Beth Ann Nichols is a senior writer for Golfweek covering the LPGA and all things women's golf. Follow her on X/Twitter (@GolfweekNichols ). item.title: How Jaden McDaniels’ $40 million contract extension is literally unprecedented
item.description: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images How Jaden McDaniels’ $40 million contract extension is literally unprecedented appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Minnesota Timberwolves standout Jaden McDaniels recently signed a one-year, $40 million extension ahead of the start of the Timberwolves season on Wednesday. The move guarantees McDaniels will remain a key member of Minnesota’s rotation for the foreseeable future, extending him through the 2029-2030 season. With the extension, he’s also made history. According to a report by Michael Scotto, McDaniels is the first player in league history to secure an extension on an already favorable contract. “ Jaden McDaniels becomes the first player in NBA history to secure an extension with three fully guaranteed seasons remaining on a non-max contract. The deal was negotiated by Nima Namakian of Innovate Sports and Bill Duffy of WME Basketball,” Scotto posted on his X account. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Timberwolves selected McDaniels with the 28th pick in the 2020 draft, and he quickly emerged into a centerpiece of the Timberwolves’ offense and defense as Minnesota has become a contender in the Western Conference with the ascension of Anthony Edwards. Last year, McDaniels averaged 14.8 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.1 steals, and 1.1 blocks per game while shooting 51.5% from the field and 41% from three. His numbers increased in the playoffs, where he averaged 16.3 points per game and shot 44% from the field. After the Timberwolves’ preseason loss to the Detroit Pistons, Anthony Edwards praised McDaniels, calling him one of the best two-way players in the game. “I think Jaden is one of the best two-way players in the NBA, if not the best…Just him getting more touches in ball screen actions, being more involved, I think he’s gonna average 20, 25 points easy because he just knows how to play the game.” Edwards, McDaniels, and the Timberwolves start their season against Giannis Antetokounmpo in the new-look Miami Heat on Wednesday. item.title: U2 return to NFL stage for Thanksgiving Eve halftime show on Netflix
item.description: U2 will play the halftime show of the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Green Bay Packers and the host Los Angeles Rams. The game takes place at SoFi Stadium on November 25 at 8pm ET, with Netflix streaming the matchup. The Irish rock band is hoping to have another "Beautiful Day" on the football field, with the booking coming nearly a quarter-century after U2 played at halftime of Super Bowl XXXVI in 2002. The performance also lands as the band marks 50 years since its formation in Dublin in 1976. Netflix has brought the star power during holiday NFL games recently. Beyonce performed at halftime of the Baltimore Ravens-Houston Texans game on Christmas Day in 2024. Last year, Snoop Dogg entertained at halftime of the Detroit Lions-Minnesota Vikings Christmas Day game. "There's a reason U2 has headlined stadiums for decades: They don't just perform, they deliver iconic moments audiences remember forever," Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos said in a statement. "We're thrilled that they'll bring that same magic to the NFL stage on Netflix." The news of U2’s return to the NFL stage comea amidst reports that Jay-Z has chosen himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show in 2027. Sources told Puck News that the rapper thought he was a more compelling pick compared to Miley Cyrus and Justin Bieber , who were both believed to be frontrunners for the event. Jay-Z’s label Roc Nation signed a deal with the NFL in 2019 to curate and produce the halftime show. Last year, Puerto Rican singer and rapper Bad Bunny headlined the show. item.title: Milan owners RedBird in talks to take control of Al-Nassr in partnership with Ronaldo
item.description: Milan owners RedBird in talks to take control of Al-Nassr in partnership with Ronaldo Tuesday’s reports claim that Milan’s ownership group RedBird capital have held talks regarding a potential purchase of a majority stake in Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr, which would also see Cristiano Ronaldo claim 20% of the shares in the club that he currently plays for. Report: Milan owners interested in acquiring Al-Nassr alongside Ronaldo According to information from Calcio e Finanza , the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), which owns 100% of the shares in Al-Nassr, are working to settle the club’s current debts, which reportedly amount to €190m ($213m, ⃁800m). TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 23: Gerry Cardinale, President of AC Milan, looks on before the Serie A match between Torino FC and AC Milan at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on August 23, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Their hope is to improve the club’s current financial situation in order to facilitate a sale to a consortium of investors led by RedBird, who also own Milan. According to the Calcio e Finanza report, RedBird have met ‘at least twice’ with representatives from the PIF, and have discussed the possibility of acquiring a 70% stake in Al-Nassr. It has been suggested that Cristiano Ronaldo could also take a 20% stake in the club that he currently plays for. Other entities, including the Saudi Media Company, are also involved in the consortium according to Tuesday’s report. RIYADH, SAUDI ARABIA – OCTOBER 12: Cristiano Ronaldo of team Al Nassr celebrates scoring their second goal during the AFC Champions League Elite game between Al Nassr and Neftchi Fargona at Al Awwal Park on October 12, 2026 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo by Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images) Calcio e Finanza claims that RedBird are prepared to invest around €238m ($267m, ⃁1bn) to acquire a 70% stake in Al-Nassr. This would give the club a total valuation of €340m ($381m, ⃁1.43bn). As things stand, negotiations are said to be at a ‘preliminary’ stage. Sources have told Calcio e Finanza that an agreement between RedBird and the Saudi PIF is not a guarantee at this stage.

item.title: Bayern assistant provides update on Kompany, Kimmich and Neuer ahead of Arsenal clash
item.description: Bayern assistant provides update on Kompany, Kimmich and Neuer ahead of Arsenal clash After missing Bayern Munich’s training session on Tuesday due to a viral infection affecting his hip, it remains unclear whether Vincent Kompany will be in the dugout for Wednesday’s Champions League clash with Arsenal. Filling in for Kompany at Tuesday’s pre-match press conference, Bayern assistant Aaron Danks provided an update on the Belgian coach’s condition. “Vincent has a viral infection. It’s important that he gets some rest. We’re monitoring the situation constantly and will see how he’s doing tomorrow. We’re in constant contact. He’s giving us his input; as for whether he’ll be able to be at the Allianz Arena tomorrow, we’ll see tomorrow," Danks said. Asked how it feels for Danks to take charge in Kompany’s absence, the 43-year-old replied: "Not much changes for me. We’re a strong coaching team; we have our processes in place. We need to keep the players’ energy levels high so they’re ready for tomorrow." Another question mark ahead of Wednesday’s game is Joshua Kimmich, who missed training on Tuesday for personal reasons. German media reported earlier on Tuesday that the 31-year-old was still expected to feature on Wednesday, but Danks left the question of his availability open. “Josh was absent today for personal reasons. I’m not sure what that will mean for tomorrow,” he said. Danks also provided an update on Manuel Neuer, who could return to the starting XI after missing the last two games with a foot injury. “We haven’t made a decision yet. Manu’s been back on the pitch for two days, which is brilliant. We’ll decide together with the coaching staff and Vincent. But it’s great to have Manu back,” Danks said. Should Neuer not be deemed fit enough to start, Jonas Urbig will be ready to deputise for the 40-year-old once again.

item.title: Former France player Petit hits out at protesters after riots
item.description: A protester holds a sign during a nationwide protest against the high cost of living. (is associated with: «Former France player Petit hits out at protesters after riots») Mathieu Pinard Baillet/Le Pictorium via ZUMA Press/dpa Former France player Emmanuel Petit has hit out at protesters in the wake of riots in Paris and other French cities. "I'd love to go out onto the streets right now and have a go at all these idiots," former World Cup and European champion Petit said in a video on Instagram. The 56-year-old said he felt "a deep anger - deep down inside me - towards people who are actually supposed to be just like me: born French. But they seem to care absolutely nothing about their French passports. I'm even convinced that they hate France." Serious riots broke out at the weekend during nationwide protests against the high cost of living in France. On Saturday alone, police arrested nearly 2,400 people. The government attributes the rioters to the far-left scene. The authorities said that young men from the suburbs arrived later to take part in looting. The suburban areas known as Banlieues are often characterized by poverty and a high proportion of residents with a migrant background. Petit, who now works as a TV pundit - and is known for his sometimes uncomfortable views - expressed his solidarity with the victims of the riots as well as the emergency services while issuing harsh criticism on the perpetrators. "They destroy everything, they set everything alight, they smash everything to pieces, they loot, they steal, they injure people, they attack them and insult them. It's always the same modus operandi: they wear balaclavas because what unites them all is cowardice." Petit said. Petit also levelled criticism at politicians, "because enough is enough. It really is enough. There's no money for the police, no money for the army, no money for hospitals and no money for schools. There's no money for anyone - except for you, the politicians." Petit added: "I am just like you: I love my country. I also love all foreigners who love my country and want to integrate. But as for everyone else, starting with the French who do not want France to remain as it is: go back to where you came from. We don't need you."

Jay Busbee Look, we all knew this season was going to be a weird one right from Week Zero, when William & Mary (my alma mater) took down Villanova after trailing by 10 in the final 53 seconds of the game. And the first two months of the season have only followed in that chaotic tradition. Let’s begin with the bad news. I said it in August, I took some heat for it in September, I reiterate it in October: Texas, Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning continue to be the season’s (if not the decade’s) biggest disappointment. Gifted with every possible opportunity, benefit of the doubt and alumni dollar in the state of Texas, the Longhorns still can’t keep from tripping over their own horns. Granted an unexpected extra play, Idaho scored from 25 yards out, then converted the 2-point conversion to vulture away a win. item.title: Giants release veteran linebacker after just 2 games
item.description: Jihad Ward | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants have released veteran outside linebacker Jihad Ward just three games after they poached him off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad. The news was first reported by NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo . Ward tied his career high with 5.0 sacks last season while playing for the Tennessee Titans, where current Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson had that job. When the Giants needed a replacement on the roster for Brian Burns, out with the season due to a torn ACL, they signed the 32-year-old Ward. He was on the active roster for three games, playing in two. In 41 defensive snaps, Ward had just one tackle. Ward was also a Giant in 2022 and 2023. He was a second-round pick by the Raiders in the 2016 NFL Draft. Releasing Ward could be the precursor to adding outside linebacker Trace Ford to the 53-man roster. Ford, 25, is out of practice squad elevations after playing in the Giants’ last three games. In 49 defensive snaps, Ford has eight tackles. He has also played 78 special teams snaps.

Gavin McKenna and Macklin Celebrini trained together during the offseason. On Tuesday, McKenna and Celebrini got to face off for the first time , while the top two picks of the 2026 NHL Draft also got to share the rink. Mason Marchment opened the scoring with a first period goal, but Auston Matthews tied the game on the power play in the second period. In the third period, the Leafs had the power play. William Nylander and Matthews found McKenna for the goal. It proved to be the game-winning goal, as the team added an empty-net goal later in the period. Now, McKenna is speaking out about coming through in big moments , per Leafs Latest. “You want to be a guy who’s known for those big moments, and when you get the opportunity to be out there on the ice, you want to make the most of it. Playing with guys like Auston and Willy brings confidence. It’s something I’ve taken a lot of passion in, trying to be known as a guy who’s able to perform in those situations,” McKenna said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) It was the first power play goal and first game-winning goal of McKenna’s career. So far, he has scored three goals and added three assists this season. Meanwhile, Matthews and Nylander have been great this year. Matthews put up three points in the game against the Sharks, bringing him to 16 total points this year. He has found the back of the net seven times while adding nine assists. Nylander has added five goals while chipping in eight helpers. McKenna’s career has already had ups and downs, including being benched against the Sabres last week. He looks to stay on the positive track on Tuesday night visiting the Columbus Blue Jackets. item.title: Rays make MLB history with 92-game streak not seen in 24 years after ALCS Game 6 win
item.description: Rays make MLB history with 92-game streak not seen in 24 years after ALCS Game 6 win originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays have beaten the Cleveland Guardians in the ALCS, and will now face the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series. In Game 6 of the ALCS, Tampa Bay got out to a lead and held on to win 7-3. Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz hit late-game homers to keep the Rays out in front of the Guardians, and in the process, help the team to extend a very impressive streak. As USA Today's Bob Nightengale highlighted, the Rays have now extended a streak to 92 games in a row in which they've won a game when leading after eight innings. MLB hasn't seen such a streak last this long since 2002. Rays make MLB history with ridiculous 92-game streak "The Tampa Bay Rays are now 92-0 when leading after 8 innings, the longest streak since the 2002 Oakland A's," Nightengale shared. It's been 24 years since MLB has seen a streak like this set. Those Athletics were one of the more interesting teams in MLB history, and this record the Rays just set has joined that A's team with some incredible history. Winning these games after having a late lead is huge, especially come the postseason. If the Rays have a lead after eight innings, all indicators are that they'll win. It's a simple premise, as opposing teams only have one inning to make up the run differential to either win or send it to extra innings for a chance of winning it all. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player But for 92 games in a row, every time the Rays have played in a game in which they've held a lead after eight innings, they've gone on to win the ballgame. In the World Series against the Brewers, Milwaukee will have to avoid being down after eight innings, because the Rays are the best team in MLB when leading after eight, and not just in 2026, but since the 2002 Athletics. Bryan Baker and the Rays' bullpen have been incredibly clutch for Tampa Bay, and add in an offense that can tack on some insurance runs, and the Rays are always well positioned to win a game in which they have a lead after eight innings. They've not lost a game in such circumstances for 92 straight games, and heading into the World Series, this is the exact kind of statistic that could be the difference between the Rays' first World Series title or another lost World Series. item.title: Two Vols earn SEC football weekly honors after Alabama win
item.description: Two Tennessee football players earned SEC weekly honors on Monday. Junior kicker Cooper Ranvier was named SEC Special Teams Player of the Week, while senior defensive end Tyree Weathersby earned SEC Defensive Lineman of the Week after the Vols defeated Alabama , 26-10, on Oct. 17. Ranvier converted 4-of-4 field goal attempts and 2-of-2 extra point attempts to finish with 14 points. He converted field goal attempts of 29, 33, 41 and 34 yards, respectively. Ranvier's four field goals were the most by a Tennessee kicker since Nov 9, 2024 against Mississippi State. Weathersby totaled four tackles, 2.5 tackles for a loss, two sacks, two sacks and one fumble recovery, while playing on 42 of Tennessee's defensive snaps. The Vols held Alabama to 54 rushing yards in the contest. Weathersby has 6.5 sacks this season, including 5.5 sacks in SEC play. His conference sack total ranks second among SEC players in league play this season. Tennessee has totaled 58 SEC weekly honors under head coach Josh Heupel . The Vols have earned nine SEC Special Teams Player of the Week honors and 10 SEC Defensive Lineman of the Week awards. item.title: How Aday Mara's height, weight, wingspan compare to Victor Wembanyama
item.description: How Aday Mara's height, weight, wingspan compare to Victor Wembanyama originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Before the 2026 NBA Draft even took place, a lot of people were high on Aday Mara out of Michigan. He is a gigantic player, so a lot of people immediately compared him to San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama. With Mara's size, the newest Oklahoma City Thunder big man was immediately billed as a potential "Wemby stopper" by people in NBA circles. It is fair to think of him like that because of his amazing physical traits that could be on par with Wembanyama, especially since they are part of teams that are each other's rivals. Comparing Aday Mara and Victor Wembanyama's height, weight, and wingspan Since 2023, Wembanyama's physical traits have been at the forefront. In the official listings, Wembanyama stands at 7'4", has a wingspan of 8'0", and weighs around 235 pounds. Considering his physical traits, a lot of people would not be surprised if he stayed under the rim, but that is not the case. Wembanyama is the league's most unique player because, with those physical traits, he can play at the perimeter just like a shooting guard or small forward. He is one of the league's anomalies because he makes everything look absurd due to his height, but he still ends up dominating the game on both ends of the floor. MORE: The reason why Aday Mara does not need any clearance from his former team to play in the NBA As showcased in the 2025-26 season, Wembanyama can carry his team to success. He is the Spurs ' biggest superstar, so he produces numbers like one. Since people see him as one of the league's biggest obstacles, other NBA teams want to compete with Wembanyama with their own giant. It seems the Thunder just got that by picking Mara, who was a standout at Michigan. Physically, he can match up to Wembanyama because he is a tad shorter at 7'3", but he does have a wingspan of 7'6" and a listed weight of around 259.8 pounds. This is certainly a fun comparison to make because Mara does have the tools to become the primary Wemby stopper. He is deceptively quick on his feet, so Wembanyama might be surprised by how quick Mara can be when playing defense. With his similar wingspan and a weight advantage, Mara has the tools to surprise Wembanyama. It will be interesting to see how they will play against each other, as Mara could be the Thunder's solution to slowing Wembanyama down after their competitive series in the 2026 Playoffs. item.description: Former Tennessee basketball star Dalton Knecht will be looking for a new home for the 2026-27 NBA season. Knecht was waived by the Los Angeles Lakers on Oct. 19 as teams shaved their rosters down to 15 players prior to the start of the season on Oct. 20. The Lakers drafted the 2024 SEC Player of the Year with the No. 17 pick in 2024. He was the highest-drafted player under Vols coach Rick Barnes before the Milwaukee Bucks selected Nate Ament at No. 13 in the 2026 NBA Draft. Here are five NBA teams where Knecht would fit best. Memphis Grizzlies A homecoming, of sorts. Knecht's best chance to stick in the NBA would mean a return to the state of Tennessee. The Grizzlies are in a full rebuild after trading Ja Morant, Jaren Jackson Jr. and sharpshooting guard Desmond Bane. They wound up at the top of the draft and selected forward Cameron Boozer. Memphis won't be in title contention this season, which would provide minutes for Knecht to get on the floor. The Grizzlies don't have a strong guard or wing rotation, and despite his shortcomings on the defensive end, Knecht is still a capable scorer at the NBA level. In his 16 starts as a rookie, the 6-foot-6 forward averaged 16.7 points on 46.1% shooting from the floor and 39.5% from 3-point range. Charlotte Hornets Knecht's career derailed early after a rescinded trade that would've sent him to Charlotte, kept him in Los Angeles. The Hornets, though, are in a similar situation to Memphis. Charlotte retooled its roster around Brandon Miller after shipping LaMelo Ball to Minnesota. Charlotte is further ahead in its rebuild than Memphis, but the Hornets are looking up at a stacked Eastern Conference with 10 playoff-caliber teams. The Hornets could use a scoring punch off the bench as they figure out how to contend with the top teams, and Knecht slides right into that role. Philadelphia 76ers Early in Knecht's rookie year with the Lakers, he erupted for 37 points in a win over the Utah Jazz. His teammate, LeBron James, famously criticized opposing NBA teams for allowing the Lakers to draft Knecht at No. 17. James is now with the Philadelphia 76ers for one last title run before he retires. The Sixers have a deeper roster and championship aspirations. However, it's unlikely that James, 41, and the oft-injured 2023 MVP Joel Embiid will play the entire 82-game regular season schedule. The Bucks have a dizzying mix of soon-to-be-traded veteran role players and unformed young talent, including Tennessee forward Nate Ament . item.title: Week 7 odds: Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Saints
item.description: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a tough road win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn’t easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It’s the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. item.title: Kevin Kisner predicts whether Brian Rolapp will allow Jon Rahm to return to the PGA Tour in 2027
item.description: Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Kevin Kisner has predicted that Brian Rolapp will resist the temptation to revive the Returning Member Program to enable Jon Rahm to make an immediate comeback to the PGA Tour. Rahm dealt LIV Golf a blow when his lawyer confirmed this month that the Spaniard does not plan to continue with the league for its relaunch in 2027. The question now is where will Rahm play his golf in 2027? Kevin Kisner doubts Jon Rahm will be able to make an immediate return to the PGA Tour The obvious answer appears to be the DP World Tour . Rahm is a member of the European circuit, with his most recent start coming at the BMW PGA Championship. However, there will be some who want to see Brian Rolapp offer the two-time major champion the chance to come back to the PGA Tour . The Returning Member Program was created in early 2026 to enable Brooks Koepka to rejoin following his departure from LIV Golf. Rahm would have been eligible to make the same move having won The Masters in 2023. However, he opted to stay put. Rolapp has recently said that there are no plans to start the program up again despite the uncertainty surrounding LIV. And speaking on the Fore Play Podcast , Kevin Kisner predicted that Rolapp will not change his mind now that Jon Rahm is leaving LIV. “I had this discussion at lunch today with some fellow tour players I played with this morning, and everyone’s all over the place on it. Nobody really knows,” he said. “My personal stance is Rolapp’s going to stick to his guns and be like, I gave you an opportunity to come back. I gave you a pathway in the off-season. You selected not to take it. Now go earn your way back onto our tour. If you want to be a full member in good status on our tour, there’s an option. You can go play the DP World Tour and earn your way back by finishing in the top 10.” What Jon Rahm said about the Returning Member Program after Brooks Koepka left LIV Golf Rolapp arguably produced a masterstroke when he unveiled the criteria that enabled Koepka to return to the PGA Tour. It ensured that LIV’s biggest stars could follow him, but did not open the door for players lower down the pecking order. When Rahm was asked about the opportunity presented in front of him, he was quick to say that he was remaining with LIV Golf. “I’m not planning on going anywhere, so very similar answer to what Bryson gave,” he said. “I wish Brooks the best, and as far as I’m concerned, I’m focused on LIV for this year and hoping my team can repeat as champs.” It was a boost for LIV that Rahm and DeChambeau decided to stay. The question many have probably wondered since is how difficult would it have been for Rahm to leave had he wanted to. It looks to be good news for Rahm’s career that he can get away from LIV, having barely been a contender in the majors since his defection in December 2023. But he may still have to be patient if he is hoping to get back to the PGA Tour in the near future.

item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
